attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Clocktower Harvest Run 5K, Saturday 14 August 2027
Applicant: Clocktower Merchants' Guild
Issue: 2.3

1. Event summary
A 5K race with 180 runners, starting at 08:00 in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. An ambulance from Halden Medical Transport is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 10 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
Should anyone require hospital treatment, the emergency services would be called in the normal way and would make the necessary arrangements for transfer, in line with their usual procedures.

5. Communications
Members of the team will have their mobile phones with them, and a list of contact numbers will be circulated in the week before the event. Coverage in the area is generally reported to be good.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Grace Lindqvist, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

Some background. Our committee has run this race for a number of years and takes the welfare of runners to heart. One of our longtime members is a retired paramedic who usually runs the race herself and is not on duty that day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Clocktower Harvest Run 5K
Date: Saturday 14 August 2027
Applicant: Clocktower Merchants' Guild
Prepared by: Brightway Traffic Consulting
Issue: 2.3

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Clocktower Harvest Run 5K, a 5K race in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden with a 08:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Signal Hill Traffic Services.
- Ash Avenue, Spring Way to Mill Road: closed 06:30 to 09:45
- Kings Parkway, Spring Way to Mill Road: closed 06:30 to 09:45
- Dyer Street, Vine Street to Spring Way: closed 06:30 to 09:45
- Glebe Road, Spring Way to Canon Road: closed 06:30 to 09:45
- Salter Way, Garrison Street to Canon Road: closed 06:30 to 09:45

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 06:30 until the last runner has passed.
- Station Road at Salter Way: 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- High Street at Dyer Street: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Ash Avenue: traffic diverted via Regent Road and Tram Street, signed from Canon Road
- Kings Parkway: traffic diverted via Dock Road and Ferry Road, signed from Vine Street
- Dyer Street: traffic diverted via Church Road and Prince Street, signed from Orchard Road
- Glebe Road: traffic diverted via Cross Avenue and Queen's Road, signed from Mill Road
- Salter Way: traffic diverted via Queen's Road and Regent Road, signed from Garrison Street

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

6. Notification
Details of the event will be published on the organiser's website and shared through social media in the weeks leading up to race day.

Some background. Our committee has run races in this part of Port Halden for a number of years, and most of our members live locally. The council's traffic controller looked over an early sketch of the route last year, though not this version of the plan.

7. Reopening
Roads will be reopened following the conclusion of the event, once barriers and equipment have been removed by the contractor.
